paper_title: Extended Axion Dark Matter Search Using the CAPP18T Haloscope
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling
notes: CAPP18T haloscope search for axion dark matter in the mass range 19.883–19.926 µeV (4.8077–4.8181 GHz). The paper reports exclusion limits on the axion-photon-photon coupling g_aγγ at 90% credibility level using Bayesian method. The limit is stated as ~0.7×|g_aγγ^KSVZ| or ~1.9×|g_aγγ^DFSZ|. The KSVZ benchmark value is approximately 5.1×10^-16 GeV^-1 in this mass range (from Figure 4), so 0.7×KSVZ ≈ 3.6×10^-16 GeV^-1. The data points represent a mass-independent (flat) bound across the scanned frequency range, encoded as two points spanning the mass interval. Local dark matter density of 0.45 GeV/cm³ (100% axions) assumed per standard halo model. No significant axion signal detected; all 20 rescan candidates failed the test. System noise temperature improved to ~0.6 K (535 mK typical) after detector reconstruction.
